facts: The paper 'The Socio-Structural Basis of the Long-Term Decline in Traditional Left-Right Class Voting in Affluent Democracies, 1964‐2019' was authored by Juan J. Fernández, Antonio M. Jaime-Castillo, and Berta Caihuelas Navajas.
The study was published in Comparative Politics on July 1, 2025 (doi:10.5129/001041525x17368768326041).
It investigates the causes behind the long-term decline in the class-based voting cleavage observed in affluent democracies since the 1960s.
The authors hypothesized that the cleavage decline connects to the shrinkage of the working class, increases in economic prosperity, and reduced inequality levels.
The analysis uses a newly assembled dataset covering sixteen advanced democracies across the period from 1964 to 2019.
Class voting was measured using an index based on the difference between a social class's proportion in a party's electorate and its proportion in the overall electorate.
Empirical models utilizing country fixed effects confirmed a widespread decline in class-based voting cleavage across Western democracies.
Controlling for several political variables, the size of the working class emerged as the best predictor of declines in class voting in affluent democracies.
